title: six playable characters and a picker
lensAText: a sceptical game art director and UX lead. For each of the six, open the reference sheets in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/0N-name/ (body-sheet.webp, face-sheet.webp) with the Read tool and compare them with the builder's renders view by view: is each character clearly recognisable as THAT person (build and height, skin tone, face shape, hair, outfit and colours, accessories), consistent with the others in style, readable at phone size, free of artefacts (gaps, clipping, z-fighting, broken hair or cloth)? Then take your own frames in ONE short Playwright script on dist/artifact.html: the picker at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3) and 1450x767; pick two different characters, walk in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (via Go To, Get out) and confirm the chosen one is the one on screen and the driving hands take their skin tone.
brief: THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~12:30 PM PT): "make there be 6 characters to choose from 3 being male and 3 female that ChatGPT can generate images for you to accurately and realistically use for this game" (later: 'realistically' means usable, not photoreal). The owner generated the reference sheets: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/ (roster.md has the names, ages, builds, outfits and notes; each 0N-name/ folder has body-sheet.webp = front/three-quarter/side/back A-pose and face-sheet.webp = front/profile/three-quarter smile). The six: 01 Mateo Reyes (27, 175 cm, stocky), 02 Danny Tran (31, 172 cm, slim, glasses), 03 Marcus Bell (38, 188 cm, muscular, shaved head, beard, scar on his RIGHT eyebrow, sunglasses on head), 04 Leila Farahani (29, 168 cm, wavy shoulder-length hair, hoops, blazer), 05 Jas Cruz (24, 160 cm, high ponytail, cropped bomber), 06 Kate Morgan (35, 175 cm, freckles, low ponytail, denim shirt, cargo pants). BUILD: (1) src/onfoot/cast.ts (new, ours): the six as presets for the existing people builder (src/onfoot/people: buildPerson, preset, PRESETS, PersonOptions, Look, Garment, Accessories), matching the sheets as closely as the stylised real-time look allows (honest: stylised 3D on a phone, not photoreal). (2) Missing builder features, ADDITIVE ONLY, in src/onfoot/people/* (agreed with the session that owns it): new hair styles (high ponytail, low ponytail, skin fade with textured top, side-part undercut, shoulder-length waves), garments (bomber, blazer, overshirt, work jacket, henley, cargo pants, chino shorts, work pants, sandals, deck shoes, low heels, chunky sneakers, boots) and accessories (glasses, sunglasses on the head, thin chain, hoop earrings, watch, hair tie) behind NEW parameter values; existing defaults, presets and the public API unchanged; avoid face.ts, masks.ts and skin.ts (another branch changes them; if a face feature truly needs them, say so instead). (3) A character picker: in the main menu or garage, six cards with each character's three-quarter smile portrait (cropped from face-sheet.webp, compressed WebP at most ~40 KB each, inlined) plus a live 3D turntable of the selected one; the choice is saved in the profile; default = keep today's player look until the player picks. (4) The chosen character is the player's avatar on foot in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (inside the game through src/onfoot/embed.ts, and the standalone pages), and the driving hands take their skin tone through the hands' public setTone(hex) (no edits to src/preview/hands*). Phone-cheap: LOD via the builder's own budget; no per-frame allocation. Our own names; no real brands or logos on clothing. ADD a regression check: the six presets build within budget, the picker saves and restores the choice, the venue avatar matches the choice, the hands' tone follows. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (owner-test mark kept); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,venues and the new check; renders of each character front/side/back beside the same views cropped from its body sheet, and the head beside the face sheet, into tests/out/cast/; picker frames at 390x844 and 1450x767; one frame of a chosen character in each venue.
